selection_framework.strength: Use exact grade, product form, heat treatment and temperature; cobalt-base alloys are not interchangeable merely because they share a nominal Co-Cr system.
selection_framework.hot_hardness: A principal advantage of several cobalt-base wear alloys is retention of hardness at elevated temperature.
selection_framework.fatigue: Assess surface condition, carbide morphology, notch sensitivity, thermal cycling, mean stress and environment.
selection_framework.fracture: Cast, hardfaced and wrought material can have materially different defect populations and fracture behaviour.
selection_framework.wear: Wear performance is strongly application-specific; hardness alone is not a sufficient wear model.
selection_framework.microstructure: Carbide type, size, distribution and matrix condition can dominate mechanical and wear behaviour.

design_rule: Never select a cobalt-base material from hardness or room-temperature tensile strength alone.
